Article Title: Mamata Banerjee's Rejinagar pick withdraws from bypolls contest, makes U-turn later
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee faces setback in Rejinagar as her candidate withdraws.

Candidate changes his mind

Nandigram setback came first

TMC split complicates bypoll battle

Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, changed his decision to quit the contest on Saturday, saying he would remain in the race after Banerjee asked him to continue.Chowdhury, a former TMC MLA, had announced his withdrawal earlier in the day, citing difficulties in protecting party workers and introducing voters to the faction's newly allotted 'footballer' symbol.Hours later, he held another press conference and said he had reversed his decision after speaking to Banerjee and receiving assurances of security from the police.Chowdhury told news agency PTI at his home in Murshidabad earlier on Saturday, "It is becoming difficult for me to motivate grassroots workers who have been facing regular harassment. Also, it is an onerous task to familiarise the electorate with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time. In this given situation, last night I informed Mamata di about my decision (not to contest)... Let's see," he said.Later, he announced that he would contest the October 6 bypoll."I will be contesting the bypoll. I have been assured of security by the police after the supremo (Banerjee) intervened... I had a conversation with our party chief, who directed me not to quit the poll fray.I have met officers of the Beldanga police station and they have also assured me and my cadre of security during campaigning.""I am retracting from my earlier decision. I will see to it that none of our workers faces torture. Even if I have 10 activists, I will win," he added.The confusion in Rejinagar came a day after the Mamata faction suffered a setback in Nandigram, where its candidate Sanchita Pradhan Dey withdrew her nomination shortly before the deadline.Dey had met West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari at the state secretariat Nabanna along with her husband Satyajit before pulling out. She had lost her job in connection with a teacher recruitment scam. The reason for her withdrawal was not immediately clear.With no candidate left, Banerjee announced support for Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, calling the Congress a "sister party" and saying the move was aimed at strengthening the INDIA bloc ahead of the October 6 bypoll.Pradhan was later arrested in connection with criminal cases filed against him during the 2007 anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram.The developments have unfolded amid a bitter dispute within the Trinamool Congress over its name and traditional 'flowers-and-grass' symbol.The Election Commission has allotted Banerjee's faction the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'footballer' symbol. The rival faction led by Arup Roy has been given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.Banerjee's camp accused the BJP government of "acting in an authoritarian manner to crush dissent and win the bypoll by a huge margin".BJP leader and Union minister Sukanta Majumdar rejected the charge, saying such allegations were expected from a "party centred on one person, whose activists had carried out attacks on the then opposition BJP after the 2021 assembly polls".With Chowdhury now back in the contest, the Mamata faction has retained its candidate in Rejinagar, while the Nandigram contest remains shaped by the withdrawal of its original nominee and its subsequent support for the Congress candidate.
Article Summary: Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, changed his decision to quit the contest on Saturday. He had announced his withdrawal earlier in the day, citing difficulties in protecting party workers and introducing voters to the faction's newly allotted 'footballer' symbol. He later announced that he would contest the October 6 bypoll.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Employees hid question papers in shoes, paid Rs 8,000 each
Article Text:

How the papers allegedly got out

Leak exposed a day before exam

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employees paid Rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by Thane City police.The chargesheet, filed before a Bhiwandi court on Friday, names 18 accused, including alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, and lays out how investigators traced the leak from the printing press to those allegedly trying to sell the papers in Maharashtra. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding, police said.According to the chargesheet, the leak was traced to Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd, an Agra-based printing press tasked with producing the confidential TET examination material.Between June 15 and 17, two employees and a former staffer allegedly concealed folded question papers inside their shoe insoles while leaving the premises. Security guards frisked their clothes but allegedly did not check their footwear, allowing the papers to be taken outside, the chargesheet said.The state had prepared four separate sets of question papers for the two TET papers to maintain confidentiality and allow one set to be selected on examination day.Investigators allege that all four sets were nevertheless taken out of the press.The employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers, according to the chargesheet.The racket came to light on June 27, a day before the TET was scheduled to be held. Deputy commissioner of Police Pavan Bansod received information that three men were allegedly trying to sell question papers to a Bhiwandi resident.Police then laid a trap using decoy personnel in Kongaon and detained the suspects, recovering four sets of question papers. Officials of the Maharashtra state council of examination later verified that the seized material matched the actual TET paper.The examination, scheduled for June 28, was subsequently postponed.Police have booked the accused under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy, along with Maharashtra laws dealing with examination malpractice. A special investigation team is probing the case.Investigators have identified Gupta, a former coaching-class teacher, as the alleged mastermind. Police said he had previously been implicated in another examination paper leak in Odisha.The chargesheet cites money trails, technical evidence and the recovery of an original question paper from the Bihar residence of a relative of Gupta as evidence in the alleged supply chain. Police said a supplementary chargesheet would be filed as the investigation continues.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles. Two employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding.

Article Text:
Koli and businessman Moninder Singh Pandher were accused in the 2006 Nithari serial killings

What happened in Nithari

NEW DELHI: Surinder Koli, who was acquitted in the last remaining case linked to the 2006 Nithari serial killings, died by suicide at a tea stall in Haridwar on Friday, police said.His body was found at a tea stall in the Bhupatwala area, near the Lal Mata temple, where he had been living and working in recent months. Police said no suicide note had been found and an investigation was under way."Police received information this morning that a person had allegedly hanged himself. Our forensic team reached the spot. At present, it appears to be a case of suicide. The body is in police custody, and the panchanama and post-mortem proceedings are underway," police told PTI videos.Koli's death comes less than a year after the Supreme Court acquitted him in the final case connected to the Nithari killings and ordered his immediate release in November 2025. He had spent nearly two decades in prison after being arrested in connection with the disappearance and killings of children and young women in Noida.Koli, who was 30 when arrested in 2006, had worked as a domestic help at the Noida home of businessman Moninder Singh Pandher . He was convicted in multiple cases and awarded several death sentences before the convictions were overturned in subsequent appeals.The Supreme Court's final acquittal brought an end to the criminal cases against him related to Nithari.The Nithari killings came to light in December 2006 after human skeletal remains were found in a drain near bungalow D-5 in Sector 31, Noida, which belonged to Pandher. The discovery followed months of complaints over missing children and young women from the area.s in the 12 cases in 2025. In November that year, it also allowed his curative petition in the final pending cThe recovery of skulls and bones triggered nationwide outrage and led to the arrest of Koli and Pandher. The case was subsequently transferred from the Uttar Pradesh Police to the CBI amid criticism of the initial investigation. CBI searches around the bungalow and adjoining areas led to the recovery of further human remains.Koli was eventually convicted in 13 cases by the trial court. However, the legal case against him unravelled over the years. In October 2023, the Allahabad High Court acquitted Koli in 12 cases and Pandher in two, citing serious shortcomings in the investigation and questioning the reliability of crucial evidence, including Koli's confession.The Supreme Court upheld Koli's acquittal, setting aside his conviction and ordering his release. The court held that the evidentiary basis for the conviction could not stand after the same evidence had been rejected in the other cases.Pandher, meanwhile, was released from prison in October 2023 after his acquittal.

His body was found at a tea stall in the Bhupatwala area, near the Lal Mata temple, where he had been living and working in recent months. Police said no suicide note had been found and an investigation was under way.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Article Summary: The Election Commission told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls remain pending. The poll panel told the apex court that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.

Article Title: Smooth take off: Pilot handles Punjab turbulence with ‘no CM face’ formula; but can he carry Congress beyond winning line?
Article Text:
Sachin Pilot with Charanjit Singh Channi and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring during a protest to demand justice for the late Gulzar Singh in Chandigarh on Tuesday.

But will Pilot’s truce hold?

Well begun is half done

“No CM face” compromise

PM Modi vs Rahul

NEW DELHI: The Congress in Punjab has finally hit the ground running. Sachin Pilot, who replaced Bhupesh Baghel as the party’s state in-charge, successfully navigated the state unit out of months of internal turmoil and ensured the party’s campaign for the 2027 assembly elections could finally take off.With arch-rivals - former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and state Congress chief Raja Warring - on board, Pilot led a mega protest demanding the resignation of Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema, who faces charges of abetment of suicide of a Dalit, Gulzar Singh.The entire state leadership and thousands of party workers marched towards Cheema’s residence. Police used water cannons to stop the protesters’ march. But the point was made. The Congress was finally in action mode.Pilot ensured that Channi and Warring, whose open power tussle has derailed Congress’s Punjab campaign, not only shared the stage but also did a “tense” handshake.Putting up a huge show of unity during the protest, Channi said, "We will fight together." Warring reciprocated. The state Congress chief called Channi and other leaders his 'pagg da lar' (the fold of his turban).Expressing gratitude to party workers for mobilising in such huge numbers at short notice, Pilot assured each one of them that the Congress will always stand by them. The Congress in-charge assured party workers that he was the representative of the high command and would not leave any stone unturned to restore the dignity and honour of every Congress worker.That’s the big question. The Punjab Congress has seen a no-holds-barred battle between Channi and Warring ever since the high command announced on July 1 that Warring would continue as Punjab Congress chief, ignoring Channi’s claims.The announcement triggered immediate protests from Channi’s supporters. They demanded that Channi should be projected as the party’s CM face in the assembly elections. What followed left the Congress leadership red-faced. From war or words to slogan-shouting at party meetings, the wide split in the state unit was out in the open. The Congress sent Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel to firefight, but he was also singed in the crossfire. Channi camp leaders accused him of siding with Warring.Pilot, who was then air-dashed to Punjab to set the house in order, has passed his maiden test. But assembly elections in the state are still at least 5 months away. Holding the rival factions together till then will indeed be a daunting challenge for the former Rajasthan deputy chief minister.So, how did Pilot cross the first hurdle smoothly? What did he do differently, which Bhupesh Baghel couldn’t?Former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel was sent to Punjab in February this year. The Congress in Punjab then was a deeply divided house. Baghel worked hard on the ground to bridge differences between the state leaders. But on July 1, when the Congress high command announced to continue with Raja Warring as the state Congress president and made Channi the head of the campaign committee, the rebellion in the state unit came out in the open.Channi’s supporters openly opposed the decision. When Baghel reinforced the leadership structure and ruled out any change, the rebels openly protested and even raised slogans against him.Baghel tried to pacify the rebels by announcing that Punjab elections would be fought under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and no state leader would be projected as CM face. But the rebels had lost his trust and refused to budge.With the rebels refusing to relent and their open infighting embarrassing the party leadership, the Congress high command decided to do a course correction to set its house in order.Baghel was shifted out, Pilot was brought in with a clear message: Congress would contest the 2027 assembly elections under collective leadership, and Rahul Gandhi would be the face of the campaign. This was a half-way compromise. The party leadership relented on Baghel but refused to budge on replacing Warring - at least for now.Warring was handpicked by the Congress high command to lead the Punjab unit after the party’s rout in the 2017 assembly elections - which saw the grand-old-party reduced to 17 assembly seats - its worst-ever performance in the state.So, Pilot has crossed the first hurdle. But at what cost? Congress’s decision to fight the Punjab assembly elections under collective leadership, with Rahul Gandhi as the face of the campaign, may have at best delayed the inevitable power tussle.But it creates another challenge for the party. Much of the Congress’s success in the state till now has been driven by a strong local leadership - Captain Amarinder Singh, who is now with the BJP.The AAP has already announced to contest the upcoming assembly elections under the leadership of Bhagwant Singh Mann. Arvind Kejriwal, who is the face of AAP has largely worked from behind the scenes - planning and strategising for the Punjab challenge. For the Akalis, Sukhbir Singh Badal is the undisputed leader and the party’s campaign revolves around him.That leaves us with the BJP and the Congress.The Congress decision to contest Punjab assembly elections with Rahul Gandhi as the party’s face makes the upcoming electoral contest interesting, and perhaps also challenging for the party.The BJP has already launched an aggressive campaign for Punjab with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the party’s campaign. PM Modi has already held two rallies in the poll-bound state and has announced a slew of development projects. As the campaign progresses, we will see the Prime Minister go all out against BJP’s political opponents. The BJP, which is in the process of building the party in the state, also has no visible local leadership. It has acquired quite a few prominent leaders from AAP and Congress, but it is unlikely any of them would be projected as the CM face. BJP’s campaigns in states are mostly centralised, with all top leaders campaigning for the party and PM Modi leading the charge. Punjab should be no exception.And that is what should worry the Congress. The fight to conquer Punjab could well become another PM Modi vs Rahul contest. In several such direct contests in the past, the Congress has struggled. However, Punjab could be different. The BJP, for a greater part of its existence in the state, has played second fiddle to the Akalis.The BJP has announced a solo contest in 2027 elections.For the Congress, Punjab has been one of the happiest hunting grounds. Despite the haunting memories of Operation Blue Star and the anti-Sikh killings, Punjab has voted for the Congress. Now, it is over to Pilot to take the Congress beyond the winning line.
Article Summary: Sachin Pilot replaced Bhupesh Baghel as the party’s state in-charge. Pilot led a mega protest demanding the resignation of Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema, who faces charges of abetment of suicide of a Dalit, Gulzar Singh.

Article Title: Mamata gets 'footballer', but can she win TMC 'khela'? Maharashtra has a red-card warning
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee faction got 'football player' as its symbol.

Mamata Banerjee is now fighting to save her own party name and symbol.

They do not know that I cannot leave TMC. It will always be with me until I leave this world. Absolutely dirty game, but we are also ready to fight it out. I want the BJP to go from India. We want solidarity in INDIA alliance. Mamata Banerjee

What Shiv Sena and NCP cases tell us

The timeline of TMC split.

The 'new' Mamata party

They had said beforehand, 'naam bhi rakhne doonga, nishaan bhi nahi rakhne doonga' (Neither let you keep the name nor the symbol). Who are these people? They are in power today; they might not be in power tomorrow. They should understand their limitations. Mamata Banerjee

Nandigram changes the bypoll test

For 28 years, TMC has been Mamata Banerjee and Mamata Banerjee has been TMC in West Bengal; the two are almost synonymous with each other. And for voters, the political shorthand for Mamata Banerjee has been almost absurdly simple: two flowers on grass.Now, that shorthand has been taken away.The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', with a football player as its symbol. The rival Arup Roy faction will contest as 'Democratic Trinamool Congress', with an 'envelope' as its symbol. The decision follows the commission's September 17 order freezing the original All India Trinamool Congress name and its reserved 'flowers and grass' symbol for the upcoming bypolls.But the EC's interim arrangement is only the first chapter. The substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.And here, the story might look familiar.The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with the Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.When Shiv Sena split between Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde in 2022, the EC first froze the party's 'bow and arrow' symbol and allotted separate interim identities to the two factions.In its February 2023 decision, the commission eventually recognised the Shinde faction as the Shiv Sena and allowed it to use the original name and symbol.The NCP followed a similar path. After Ajit Pawar's rebellion in July 2023, the EC decided in February 2024 that the faction led by Sharad Pawar had a weaker numerical claim, while Ajit Pawar's group had superior support in the organisational and legislative wings. It consequently recognised Ajit Pawar's faction as the NCP and allowed it to use the party's 'clock' symbol. The EC order specifically recorded that the Ajit Pawar group had "far superior numerical support" in the organisational and legislative wings.That is a crucial part of the precedent for the ongoing TMC dispute.The conclusion from the Maharashtra cases may be that the EC followed the majority of legislators. The legal position is more nuanced. Paragraph 15 allows the election commission to examine rival claims through the party's organisational structure as well as its legislative strength.In its May 11, 2023 Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai vs Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra, the Supreme Court held that the EC need not determine a party's identity solely through the numerical strength of its MLAs or MPs while adjudicating a dispute under Paragraph 15 of the Symbols Order. The court said the EC could consider the majority in the organisational wing, the party constitution and, where appropriate, "any other appropriate test", underlining that a split among legislators is not necessarily the same as a split in the political party itself.The observation is particularly relevant to the TMC case, where the eventual contest could involve competing claims over the party's organisational structure and not just a headcount of elected representatives. The Supreme Court, however, did not itself decide which faction should receive the Shiv Sena's name and symbol, leaving the merits of that EC decision to separate proceedings.That distinction could matter considerably in the TMC case.The Shiv Sena and NCP rebels who ultimately secured the original party identities had substantial support among sitting legislators. The TMC's internal arithmetic, however, has to be examined on its own terms.The 2026 assembly election setback changed the party's internal arithmetic sharply. Its tally fell from 215 of 294 seats in 2021 to 80, and within weeks, 58 MLAs backed expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee as their legislature party leader. He was subsequently recognised as leader of the opposition, while the rebel camp rejected Mamata's nominee, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay.The revolt then spread to Parliament, with 20 Lok Sabha MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar joining the NCPI and backing the BJP-led NDA. The TMC challenged their move before the Lok Sabha speaker and sought their disqualification. What began as a post-election leadership challenge had thus expanded into a contest over control of the party's legislative and parliamentary wings.Mamata Banerjee, however, remains the founder and central political figure of the organisation, and her camp's claim is not based only on her position as party leader but also on its organisational and electoral support.The names allotted on Friday were revealing because neither faction chose to abandon the Trinamool identity. Mamata's camp was given 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', while the rival Arup Roy camp became 'Democratic Trinamool Congress'. Both were, in different ways, laying claim to continuity with the party Mamata Banerjee founded on January 1, 1998.The distinction lies in the source of legitimacy each side is emphasising. The rebels' use of 'Democratic' fits their argument that the TMC's organisational functioning should be more representative and less centred around one leader. Mamata's faction, meanwhile, has effectively put the founder's name where the old party identity used to be, making 'Mamata' part of its temporary electoral brand. That is particularly striking for a party whose political identity has been inseparable from its founder for almost three decades.The football-player symbol allotted to Mamata's faction also carries its own political resonance in Bengal. Football has long had a deep cultural presence in the state, but there is also a direct connection to the TMC's campaign vocabulary: 'Khela Hobe', the slogan that became a defining part of Mamata's 2021 assembly campaign against the BJP.The symbol does not automatically recreate that campaign, but it gives the Mamata faction a ready-made visual association at a time when it has lost the party symbol voters have known for nearly three decades.The test, however, has now changed in a rather dramatic way for the Mamata faction.Mamata faction's candidate, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination from the Nandigram contest altogether, a day before the deadline. Her withdrawal came minutes after she met West Bengal chief minister and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, although the circumstances surrounding the meeting and her decision remain a matter of political speculation.Mamata Banerjee later announced in a press conference that her party will now back the Congress candidate in Nandigram, and mentioned that the decision was taken "for the greater interest of the nation" and to strengthen the INDIA bloc."Rahul Gandhi rang me up yesterday, Arvind Kejriwal also expressed solidarity; we will all fight together against BJP. We will support Congress in the Nandigram bypoll to strengthen the INDIA bloc," Mamata said. The Congress candidate, however, was also arrested by the cops late in the evening in a land-grab case.That makes the October 6 bypolls a very different test from the one that appeared possible 24 hours earlier. The Mamata faction will now not be testing its new 'football-player' identity in Nandigram, but instead, ask its supporters to transfer their support to a Congress candidate, even as the rival TMC faction contests the seat under its own new identity.The political significance is difficult to miss. At precisely the moment when the EC has stripped Mamata's faction of the old TMC name and symbol and given it a new identity, the faction is now out of a direct fight in Nandigram, a constituency that carries an unusually strong personal history for both Mamata and Suvendu Adhikari.Nandigram was where Mamata lost to Adhikari in the 2021 assembly election, after making the constituency the centrepiece of her campaign. Adhikari, who had moved from the TMC to the BJP before that election, defeated her by a narrow margin in a contest that became one of the defining episodes of Bengal politics. He subsequently retained Nandigram while also winning Bhowanipore, which he vacated to retain Nandigram, necessitating the October 6 bypoll.The EC may eventually decide who owns the TMC name and symbol, but the October 6 bypolls will offer the first test of how much of the old Trinamool identity survives without 'flowers and grass'. In Rejinagar, the football player and envelope will face each other directly; in Nandigram, Mamata's decision to back Congress will test whether her political support can travel even when her own new party name and symbol are not on the ballot.
Article Summary: The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' But the substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided. The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.

Article Title: When the mullai refused to bloom
Article Text:
“Mullaiyum Pooththiyo, Ollaiyur Naade?”

“Vaiyaththul Vaazhvaangu Vaazhpavan Vaanuraiyum

Theyvaththul Vaikkap Padum.”

He embodied it.

On the day Pappaiah sir was laid to rest, there was orderliness at the church, and all the way to the burial ground. But as the van entered the cemetery, a sea of cameras took over. His family, and those of us from his intimate literary circle, could not go near him. I could not get a last glimpse the doyen of Tamil Pattimandram and connoisseur of literature. He left without our goodbye.On our way to the airport, a flower vendor tapped on our car window. In her hands was a bunch of maruda malli. The flowers looked wilted. A Sangam poem by Kudavayil Keerathanar came to my mind. After mourning Sathan, his patron, the poet, on entering Ollaiyur and seeing the mullai blooming, asks the flower why, when no one in the grieving land will wear it:I looked at the wilted flowers and thought: How could flowers bloom in Madurai on the day a great son of its soil was being laid to rest?Grief has a physical weight. At first, memories flood. Then life resumes its ordinary rhythm, only to ambush us at unexpected moments. Some of us had the rare privilege of spending hours with him, seeing the man beyond the stage—his humility.Years ago, when I joined his team and the celebrated Pattimandram on Sun TV , a few jealous voices tried to push me out. A sentence I had casually uttered was relayed to him as an “objectionable” remark, and I was told that affected parties might send a legal notice to me and to him as moderator.My life on stage was over, I thought. But he looked at the person who had brought him the news and said, “It looks like you are the affected party who has staged this.”That day I learnt something precious: he could be formidable when protecting those entrusted to him. He was not merely a judge of debates; he was a discerning judge of people.I learnt about simplicity from him too. At functions, the rich and powerful would surround him for photographs. But his eyes would seek the drivers, cleaning women and security guards standing at a distance, and he would walk towards them and ask for a picture.His greatest literary contribution was taking the Thirukkural into ordinary homes. For more than seven years, he travelled almost every week from Madurai to Chennai, often by train, to record a Kural a day for Sun TV, beginning with his unforgettable, “Loving mothers, revered elders and sweet children.” Ancient wisdom entered countless contemporary lives.I met him at Sivakasi just five days before he passed away. He was as vibrant as ever. The topic was Gen Z. We wondered how he would connect with them. He did more than connect. He spoke their language and gave his verdict in their favour.He seemed to be passing on the mantle.He went home that day and never returned to the stage.No prolonged hospitalisation. No dependence. A dignified life, followed by a dignified death.And in death, he brought alive Kural 50:One who lives an ordained life in this world, Is placed among the divine.Pappaiah sir did not merely explain that Kural.
Article Summary: Pappaiah sir was the doyen of Tamil Pattimandram and connoisseur of literature. His greatest literary contribution was taking the Thirukkural into ordinary homes. For more than seven years, he travelled almost every week from Madurai to Chennai, often by train, to record a Kural a day.

Article Title: ‘Unconstitutional, illegal, undemocratic’: Mamata after EC assigns new symbol and name
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee addressing a press conference

Mamata backs Congress in Nandigram

Mamata alleges ‘vote theft’

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Friday called the developments surrounding the Trinamool Congress ’ internal factional dispute a “black day” in India’s democratic history, after her camp’s Nandigram bypoll candidate withdrew her nomination.Addressing a press conference, Mamata said her camp did not disrespect the Constitutional Chair but alleged that the developments were “unconstitutional, illegal, undemocratic and a totally biased vendetta to satisfy the ego of a political party”.“We don't disrespect the Constitutional Chair, but we feel today is a black day in our democratic history. What is happening in our country is very unfortunate, unconstitutional, illegal, undemocratic and a totally biased vendetta to satisfy the ego of a political party,” she said.Mamata also alleged that there had been an earlier warning that her faction would not be allowed to retain its party name and symbol.“They had said beforehand, ‘naam bhi rakhne doonga, nishaan bhi nahi rakhne doonga’. Who are these people? They are in power today, they might not be in power tomorrow. They should understand their limitations,” she said.The comments came after Sanchita Pradhan Dey, the Nandigram bypoll candidate of the Mamata Banerjee camp, withdrew her nomination on Friday, a day before the deadline for withdrawal.The development followed an interim Election Commission order freezing the use of the All India Trinamool Congress name and its traditional twin-flowers-on-grass symbol by both rival factions.The EC subsequently allotted the Mamata Banerjee-led faction the name “Mamata All India Trinamool Congress” and the symbol “Football Player”, to be treated as a recognised political party in West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.The group led by Arup Roy was allotted the name “Democratic Trinamool Congress” and the symbol “Envelope”.Dey had filed her nomination from Nandigram as the candidate of the Mamata Banerjee-led faction, accompanied by former state minister Akhil Giri.Earlier on Friday, Dey also met West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari in Kolkata.With Saturday being the last date for withdrawal of nominations, the meeting came amid the reshaping of the electoral contest.Mamata said her camp would now support the Congress in Nandigram as well as Assam .""They do not know that I cannot leave All India Trinamool Congress. It will always be with me until I leave this world...Absolutely dirty game but we are also ready to fight it out. I want the BJP to go from India. We want solidarity in INDI Alliance...In Nandigram, we are going to give our support to Congress party. It is for the greater interest of the country. Rejinagar, I will decide later. In Assam, we are not contesting..."," she said.Speaking about what she described as “vote theft”, Mamata accused the BJP of undermining democratic institutions and said the issue was a matter of “great sadness”."It is a matter of great sadness. They looted in Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Bengal. This 'Jhootha BJP Party', a 'Jumla Party'...Its job is to end democracy, Constitution and education system in the country. Even journalists are not spared; if someone speaks out against them, they are arrested.Before us, Uddhav Thackeray faced the same thing. I have no respect for any individual person who is busy only to satisfy the ego of BJP. .." she said.The developments follow the Election Commission’s interim order that froze the use of the Trinamool Congress’ traditional name and symbol by both factions, resulting in separate names and symbols being assigned to the rival groups.
Article Summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee called the developments surrounding the Trinamool Congress'internal factional dispute a 'black day' in India's democratic history. Her camp’s Nandigram bypoll candidate withdrew her nomination on Friday.

Article Title: Trapped in traffic: Exam-bound kids take 2.5 hours to cover 4km in Bengaluru
Article Text:
Schoolchildren faced severe traffic delays on the Varthur-Gunjur stretch.

Poll Vote & Share your view What's the main reason you believe traffic is so congested in the area during school hours? Poor infrastructure Heavy vehicle movement Lack of traffic management 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BENGALURU: Hundreds of school-children commuting along the Varthur-Gunjur stretch of SH-35 endured a harrowing Thursday as severe traffic congestion delayed school buses by up to 40 minutes in the morning and left students stranded on roads for hours while returning home. A 4km drive took 2.5 hours, stuck mostly in traffic.The stretch hosts 18-20 big schools, with many conducting mid-term examinations. Parents told TOI children reached exam halls anxious after school buses arrived late at pickup points and were subsequently caught in gridlocked traffic.The evening commute was worse. Several students took up to 1.5 hours more to return home. Some schools accommodated affected students by providing extra time to complete exams.The Varthur-Gunjur stretch, part of SH-35, is undergoing infrastructure works being executed by Karnataka Road Development Corporation. However, residents say the corridor continues to be plagued by bottlenecks, damaged road surfaces, large craters and unmanaged traffic, making the daily commute unpredictable. Parents said Thursday’s situation highlighted how ongoing infrastructure issues were directly affecting schoolchildren.Priti Singh, a resident of Candor Landmark Apartments, said the biggest concern was that schools had exams. “It is unbelievable an area contributing significantly to the city’s economy continues to suffer from such poor infrastructure,” she added.Another resident, Pavitra Holla, said children were spending more time in traffic than in classrooms. “Today, some children took nearly 2.5 hours to cover just 4km from school. They are exhausted, parents are worried and there is no end in sight. There are no proper roads, heavy vehicles move during school hours, traffic management is absent and basic infrastructure is missing. Children are forced to sit in dust and traffic for hours,” she said. Holla added that while congestion has been a long-standing issue in the area, conditions have deteriorated in the past two weeks.For some parents, the situation left them with little choice but to abandon school buses and attempt the journey themselves.Swati Kumari, another resident of Candor Landmark, said she waited nearly 45 minutes for her son’s school bus before deciding to take him on a two-wheeler. “My son studies in a school less than 2km away from home. Though his school ends by 2.45pm, he’s been reaching home around 4.30pm in the past month. The scooter ride took me more than an hour to travel barely 1km,” she said.Calling the commute unsafe, Kumari said parents are increasingly worried about putting young children on two-wheelers given recent accidents and the condition of the road.
Article Summary: Severe traffic congestion delayed school buses by up to 40 minutes in the morning. A 4km drive took 2.5 hours, stuck mostly in traffic. The stretch hosts 18-20 big schools, with many conducting mid-term examinations. Parents said Thursday’s situation highlighted how ongoing infrastructure issues were directly affecting schoolchildren.

Article Title: Paralympic star Lauren Steadman seals Celebrity MasterChef crown after nail-biting finale
Article Text:
Lauren Steadman. Image via: BBC

Lauren Steadman beats Celebrity MasterChef rivals in dramatic final showdown

Lauren Steadman's Celebrity MasterChef win adds to a long sporting résumé

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lauren Steadman has won Celebrity MasterChef, and the Paralympic champion needed every single course to do it. Three finalists cooked a three-course meal for judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli on Friday night, and only one could lift the 2026 trophy.The BBC One final capped a contest that began with 15 celebrities. Olympic medallist Emily Campbell and Love Island's Shakira Khan pushed hard, and Dent found the choice close to impossible. One dessert tipped the verdict, though, and a runner-up had a joke ready afterwards.Lauren Steadman took the title on Friday, September 18, in a final shown on BBC One and iPlayer at 8 p.m. The Paralympic gold medallist beat Campbell and Khan in a head-to-head where each finalist had to cook and present a faultless three-course meal. It was the last chance to show passion and creativity in front of Dent and Locatelli, and Steadman's execution earned her the trophy.Steadman opened with scallops pan-fried in chilli butter, served with a coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and topped with fresh apple batons. The main was a beef wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallot, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and a red wine jus. Dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream.The pudding did the most damage. Locatelli said, "Mamma mia... this is the best sticky toffee pudding I've ever had." Dent went with "exemplary" for the same dish and said the final plates were simply wonderful. Locatelli also explained the bigger picture. Steadman has a knack for turning every situation into an advantage, and that is why the crown went to the champion.Finals week added plenty of pressure. Steadman made a dog bone shaped dessert for fifty guests at Crufts, billed as the world's largest and most prestigious dog show. The Chef's Table at The Ritz, a top event on the culinary calendar, was another test.After the win, Steadman said, "This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal." Speechless moments are rare, Steadman added, and this was one of them.Steadman is an MBE, was born in Peterborough and is a University of Portsmouth graduate. Swimming came first, at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics at age 15 and again at London 2012. Paratriathlon followed, bringing silver in Rio 2016, gold in Tokyo and bronze in Paris 2024. The three-time world champion is also an eight-time European champion.Steadman reached the Strictly Come Dancing semi-finals in 2018 as the show's first female contestant with a disability, then finished as a finalist on Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins in 2019.The kitchen was a different kind of risk, and Steadman knew it. Before the series, the athlete told the BBC that sport had taught pressure handling and a love of new challenges. Cooking for loved ones is one thing, Steadman said, and having food critically analysed is another. The show could go very wrong, but it might also build confidence. Steadman calls the style intuitive. A soup that got far too many stock cubes once became a pasta sauce, and measuring is rarely part of the routine.The other finalists took defeat well. Campbell called the result "more than deserved" and joked about being relieved that the contest was over. Khan, a runner-up on Love Island last year, said, "Always the bridesmaid, never the bride." She added that she had a ball and called Steadman's cooking a gold medal performance.
Article Summary: Paralympic gold medallist Lauren Steadman wins Celebrity MasterChef 2026. Steadman beat Olympic medallists Emily Campbell and Shakira Khan in a head-to- head. The three-time world champion is also an eight-time European champion. The BBC One final capped a contest that began with 15 celebrities.

Article Title: At 13, Quimcy Dsouza was a middle-distance runner before football took over; 11 years later, Ronaldinho-inspired Teqball has put her one win away from Asian Games history
Article Text:
India's Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza (Image: @quimcyyy/Instagram)

From middle-distance running to football and Teqball

Seven-time national champion and international trailblazer

Quimcy Dsouza ’s Asian Games 2026 campaign

Quimcy falls short in semifinal against Indonesia

Bronze medal match offers chance to make history

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles Teqball semifinal at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday. However, her medal hopes remain alive, with the 24-year-old set to compete for bronze against Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto on Sunday.A victory would make Quimcy the first Indian to win a Teqball medal at the Asian Games, where the sport is making its debut at the Aichi-Nagoya edition. The Indian’s journey to the last four has already been a breakthrough, marking an important chapter in her rise as one of the country’s leading Teqball players.Hailing from Mumbai, Quimcy began her sporting journey as a middle-distance runner at the age of 13 as reported by The Indian Express. Her passion for football soon took over, and she went on to represent Maharashtra in age-group football.Although her football career did not progress as she had hoped, her love for the game remained. After completing a degree in Sports Management, she joined sports goods retailer Decathlon and discovered Teqball after watching Brazilian football legend Ronaldinho play the sport in Instagram videos.Quimcy took up the sport and gradually established herself as a leading figure in India’s Teqball community.Quimcy became the first Indian woman Teqer to represent the country at the international level. She also founded the Teqball Club of Bengaluru to help promote the sport at the grassroots level.A seven-time national champion, she has emerged as one of the trailblazers of Indian Teqball. Earlier in 2026, she finished ninth at the Teqball World Championships in Romania, further strengthening her credentials on the international stage. Her performances at the Asian Games have now given her an opportunity to add a historic medal to her achievements.Quimcy made an impressive start to her Asian Games debut, topping Group A with two wins to secure direct qualification for the women’s singles semifinals.She opened her campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over top-seeded Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto. After losing the first set 10-12, Quimcy fought back to win the second 12-11 before clinching the decider 13-11. She then defeated Cambodia’s Koemyean DY 12-9, 12-7 in straight sets to finish at the top of her group and book a place in the last four.Quimcy started her semifinal against Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya on a strong note, winning the opening set 12-7. Sumaya responded in the second, recovering from an early deficit to take it 12-9 and force a decider.The Indian raced to a 3-0 lead in the third set and extended it to 4-1. However, Sumaya mounted a comeback, took control of the decider and won it 12-7 to secure her place in the final. The defeat ended Quimcy’s hopes of reaching the gold-medal match, but she will have another opportunity to finish her debut Asian Games campaign on the podium.Quimcy will face Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto in Sunday’s bronze-medal match. The Indian had defeated Sakamoto in the group stage, but will need to reproduce that performance to secure a place on the podium.A win would earn India its first-ever Teqball medal at the Asian Games. Quimcy has also competed in mixed doubles alongside Mohamed Anas Imran Beg. The Indian pair defeated the Philippines’ Jhoana Abulencia and Prince Agustin in their Group A opener.Teqball, invented in Hungary, combines elements of football and table tennis and is played on a curved table. The sport is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, with five medal events: men’s and women’s singles, men’s and women’s doubles, and mixed doubles.
Article Summary: Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza lost 1-2 to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in semifinal of Teqball. The 24-year-old will now compete for bronze against Japan's Yuina Sakamoto. Quimcy is a seven-time national champion and an international trailblazer. The sport is making its debut at the Aichi-Nagoya edition.

Article Title: New Lakers owners project an astonishing $30 billion valuation in a decade as Luka Doncic’s roster prepares to enter new NBA season
Article Text:
Lakers’ new owners project $30 billion valuation within 10 years. Image via: Getty Images

New Lakers owners expect $30 billion valuation in a decade

Luka Doncic is ready to enter new NBA season with Lakers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The new Lakers owners are telling investors the team's valuation will reach at least $30 billion by the end of 2037. Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger led the group that bought the franchise for a record $12.5 billion last month, so the pitch aims high, and parts of it will land hard with fans.Across the Atlantic, Luka Doncic is finishing his offseason work in Slovenia, and the latest report on the guard's conditioning is encouraging. Lakers camp opens Sept. 29, less than two weeks away, and the early numbers point the right way.Joshua Kushner's investment firm, Thrive Capital, built the presentation, and the Wall Street Journal reviewed a copy. It says the Lakers could be worth at least $30 billion by the end of 2037. Television and streaming rights would have to double in value over the same stretch.Revenue is the other half of the story. The pitch says the Lakers are on pace to bring in $681 million this year. Ten years from now, the target is at least $1.6 billion. If conditions break even better, the group reportedly sees a long-term value of $62 billion.Per Yahoo Sports, the $30 billion mark is bigger than the latest Sportico valuations of the Trail Blazers, Timberwolves, Magic, Pistons, Hornets, Pelicans and Grizzlies combined.The owners can also point to some history. Forbes projected the Lakers at $3 billion in 2016, and the $12.5 billion sale price is roughly four times that.The presentation reportedly targets $150 million in extra revenue by 2028. Part of it would come from taking back about 6,000 season tickets now held by brokers and selling them as single-game seats, which would lift the average single-game price from $217 to $361. The owners also reportedly see $40 million to $75 million in new sponsorship money and at least $20 million in operating savings. Yahoo Sports summed it up as pricier tickets, more ads and deeper spending cuts.In public, the owners have promised to "compete at the highest level" and to serve the team, its fans and the city. Thrive also expects the NBA's media deals, now worth $77 billion over 11 years, to double when the current agreement ends.Luka Doncic has spent the offseason getting his body back in order, and the early signs are good. SportKlub.si, a Slovenian outlet, reports that the Lakers guard weighs about 105 kilograms (231 pounds) as the last stage of the Ljubljana workouts begins. BasketNews passed the report along on Sept. 15. SportKlub put it this way: "His weight is also within the desired range, unofficially even at 105 kilograms."The Lakers listed the 27-year-old at 104 kilograms (230 pounds) last season, so the gap is about one kilogram before camp even starts.Doncic suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain late last season. The injury ended the season and kept him out of the entire Lakers playoff run. The offseason plan began with rehab and then moved into conditioning work.The layoff is a long one. From the final game of last season to the first game of 2026-27, 203 days will pass. It is the longest basketball break of the Slovenian star's career.Doncic did not play for Slovenia this summer and chose family time instead. Basketball still stayed on the schedule. Individual work continued, and Doncic organized a Lakers minicamp in Slovenia.Doncic is expected to stay in Europe until Sept. 20 before flying back to Los Angeles. The Lakers hold media day on Sept. 28, and training camp opens the next day.
Article Summary: Lakers' new owners expect $30 billion valuation in a decade. Luka Doncic is finishing his offseason work in Slovenia. Lakers camp opens Sept. 29, less than two weeks away. The group that bought the franchise for a record $12.5 billion last month.

Article Title: “If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him”: Newly minted FBI special agent Shaquille O’Neal targets Inside the NBA co-host to put behind bars in a humorous jab
Article Text:
Shaquille O'Neal targets Charles Barkley. Image via: Getty Images

Shaquille O'Neal targets Charles Barkley in his honorary FBI special agent speech

Shaquille O'Neal's law enforcement ties run back two decades

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Shaquille O'Neal picked up an honorary FBI special agent title, and the four-time NBA champion wasted no time putting it to use. He graduated alongside 265 law enforcement officials at the FBI National Academy's Session 299 in Quantico, Virginia, then closed his speech with a warning aimed squarely at his longtime broadcast partner.FBI Director Kash Patel handed O'Neal the recognition once the ten-week program wrapped. O'Neal turned the moment into a shot at Charles Barkley , the co-host he has jabbed at on Inside the NBA since 2011, telling the room what to do if they ever ran into him.Shaquille O'Neal's parting line was simple. "If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him," he said, in video shared by Legion Hoops as he wrapped his remarks Thursday. The crowd of graduating officers, all veterans of their own departments, got the joke instantly given O'Neal and Barkley's decade-plus history of ribbing each other on air.Patel had announced the honor on X a day earlier, calling O'Neal "one of the best supporters of law enforcement in the country" as he presented the plaque. The title carries no real authority. It does not make O'Neal a sworn agent or give him powers of arrest, and the National Academy itself runs separately from the FBI's actual new-agent training pipeline. It exists mainly for experienced law enforcement leaders, covering leadership, academics and physical fitness over ten weeks in Quantico.This is not O'Neal dabbling. He was sworn in as a Miami Beach reserve police officer in 2005, not long after serving in the same capacity with the Los Angeles Port Police. That same year, during his reserve training, he tailed a car whose passengers had thrown a bottle at two pedestrians, then radioed dispatch so officers could track down the suspect. He later took on a reserve role in Doral, Florida, and was named Henry County Police Department's community relations chief last year.Orlando drafted him first overall in 1992, and he spent 19 seasons across six teams, winning three titles with the Lakers and one with the Heat, taking home MVP honors in 2000 and making 15 All-Star teams before his 2016 Hall of Fame induction. But the badge, honorary or not, fits a pattern he has kept up since long before Inside the NBA made him a household name twice over.As for Barkley, he has not responded publicly yet. Given their on-air history, a comeback is probably just a matter of time.
Article Summary: Shaquille O'Neal received an honorary FBI special agent title. The four-time NBA champion used the honor to take a shot at Inside the NBA co-host Charles Barkley. The title carries no real authority and does not give him powers of arrest. But it fits with a pattern of honoring law enforcement.

Kansas City's defense turned heads in Week 1 against Denver, and not just because of the outcome. The story was who was doing the damage. Several young, first-year players showed up ready, contributing in ways that had ESPN analyst Daniel Jeremiah reaching for superlatives after reviewing the film. With the Colts coming up next on the schedule, that rookie-fueled unit is already generating serious conversation around the league.The short answer, according to Jeremiah, is coaching. But it goes deeper than that."I thought the Chiefs' defense, when you dug in and watched the tape with so many new pieces and young pieces, I thought they played outstanding," Jeremiah said on ESPN's BigDay show. "From R Mason Thomas off the edge, Peter Woods inside. You saw [Mansoor] Delane with a pick before he got injured. A lot of young pieces, and this has long been one of the best teaching staffs in the NFL. And Steve Spagnolo and that group did a good job getting those young guys ready to go. So I'm a believer in this Chiefs defense."That last line matters. Jeremiah is not someone who hands out compliments loosely, especially this early in a season. What he saw on tape was not raw talent masking poor technique.These were young players executing within a system, which is a credit to how Kansas City's staff builds its install process from the ground up.Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnolo have built a culture around detailed preparation. Rookies in Kansas City do not get eased in quietly. They get pushed into the fire with enough coaching support behind them that they rarely get burned badly. It is a model that has paid off repeatedly, and Week 1 showed it is still working.That is the real question hanging over this team right now. Performing well in Week 1 is one thing. Doing it across 17 games with a roster carrying this much youth on the defensive side is something else entirely.Mansoor Delane's injury is already a concern. He picked off a pass before leaving the game, and losing a young corner with that kind of instinct is not something you shrug off. The Chiefs will need other pieces to hold up.On the offensive side, Jeremiah noted that things were not completely smooth either. "Offensively, yes, they ran the ball well, particularly from under center," he said. "I don't think the pass game was super synced up yet. Kenneth Walker III had a strong showing, and Patrick Mahomes will sharpen as the weeks go by. Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 3: Koneru Humpy downs 'Greek Goddess' Tsolakidou; Gukesh back above 2700
Article Text:
Koneru Humpy and Gukesh (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz and Michal Walusza from FIDE)

Gukesh back to winning ways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's winning streaks stay intact

NEW DELHI: On Friday, the Indian women's team, defending champions and unbeaten so far in the tournament, was paired against Greece in Round 3 of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. On paper, this looked routine. India, the top seeds, were expected to win the tie, and they eventually did. But the top-board clash between Koneru Humpy and Greece's Stavroula Tsolakidou carried a subplot that had been building for a fortnight, and it turned an otherwise straightforward fixture into the day's most closely watched game.Tsolakidou was part of Ganges Grandmasters, the eventual champions of the just-concluded Global Chess League (GCL) Season 4 . It was against Humpy, playing for APL Pipers, that Tsolakidou suffered her first loss of that tournament, playing white.To turn the tables in the reverse fixture, she needed something special, and got it when coach Adhiban Baskaran handed her a folder titled "Prep for the Greek Goddess!" Working off that file, she beat Humpy with the black pieces. The moniker "Greek Goddess" became famous.The two met again in the GCL final, where Tsolakidou held Humpy to a draw in the first game and then beat her again with black in the second.A positive score over the Indian, coupled with the results on the other boards, was enough to hand Ganges Grandmasters the title, with Tsolakidou also named the Player of the Tournament.So when the pairing brought them together again on Friday, it was more than a Grandmaster-versus-International Master matchup. This time, as the format shifted from rapid to classical, the Indian veteran Grandmaster prevailed.39-year-old Humpy, with white, built her position with patience. The game began as a Nimzo-Indian structure, with Humpy choosing an ambitious setup featuring 10.b4 and 11.b5, gaining queenside space.Black’s pieces became somewhat passive, while White gradually built pressure with 14.f4, 15.Qf3 and 16.Rad1.The critical phase arrived with 21.e5, opening lines and increasing the activity of White’s pieces.After 22.bxc6 bxc6, Humpy’s knight penetrated with 23.Ne4 and 24.Nxd6, winning material and creating tactical threats.The sequence 25.Nxe8 Rxe8 26.Qxh4 left White with a significant advantage, although Black’s active queen and passed-pawn kept the doors slightly open for a comeback.Humpy maintained the initiative, coordinating her rooks and bishop. 40.e6 was particularly strong, leading to 41.Bxe6+ and 42.Rd7+.After winning the f5-bishop with 43.Bxf5, White’s material and attacking advantage became decisive. Tsolakidou resigned after 46.Rf1, capping off a perfect day for the Indian Grandmaster, who had taken a rest against Finland in Round 2.In the open section, world champion D Gukesh made his way back to winning ways after Thursday's rating dip below 2700, a drop that had made headlines less for its size than for whom it happened to.Playing black against Italy's Sabino Brunello on Friday, Gukesh met a Queen's Indian-style setup.After 4...Ba6 and 5...c5, Black immediately challenged White’s queenside structure and achieved active piece play. The game became highly tactical once Gukesh expanded with 15...g5 and centralized strongly with 17...Ne4 and 19...Nd4.Brunello tried to simplify with 21.Nxd4 and 22.Rxc8, but Black’s pieces remained more active. The key sequence began with 23...Nc3, forcing exchanges that improved Black’s bishop activity. After 25...Re5, Gukesh increased the pressure, and 26...Bxe2 won an important pawn while keeping White’s king exposed.28...Bxh3 removed a key defender, while 29...Bd4+ and 30...Re2+ drove the king into a dangerous position. 31...Qxh3 left Black with overwhelming attacking threats and a large material advantage.Although Brunello gave checks with 32.Qxg5+ and 33.Qd8+, they were only temporary. Gukesh's queen and bishop combined to set up mating threats, and Brunello resigned after 33 moves, handing Gukesh a much-needed win and, with it, a step back towards the 2700 mark he had slipped under just a day earlier.The rest of India's open team also had a strong day against Italy. Praggnanandhaa and Erigaisi both drew their games, but Nihal Sarin added another win to his growing tally, beating Francesco Sonis, as India closed out the match 3-1.For India's women, Friday's 3.5-0.5 win over Greece, with only Divya Deshmukh drawing her game against Anastasia Avramidou, kept an already imposing unbeaten run alive, with Humpy, Vantika Agrawal, and Savitha Shri all winning their individual games. Vaishali Rameshbabu took a rest day.ALSO READ: The silver medal Koneru Humpy's 9-year-old daughter will remember as gold Both Indian teams will be back in action on Saturday, with the open side facing Spain and the women's team taking on Mongolia.
Article Summary: India's Koneru Humpy beats Greece's Stavroula Tsolakidou in Round 3 of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The Indian veteran Grandmaster prevailed as the format shifted from rapid to classical. World champion D Gukesh made his way back to winning ways after Thursday's rating dip below 2700.

Bengal cricketer Abishek Porel has been granted bail by a Chinsurah court after spending more than a month in custody in connection with an alleged rape and criminal intimidation case. The development was reported by ABP Ananda, while multiple reports have also confirmed the bail order.Porel, who plays for Delhi Capitals in the IPL, was arrested on August 11 following a complaint filed by a medical student from Karnataka. She alleged that she had been in a relationship with Porel for around three-and-a-half years and that the two had planned to marry.The complainant also alleged that they had travelled abroad together during their relationship, but claimed that Porel later denied their relationship, prompting her to approach the police.Her complaint was filed at Mogra police station on June 23. She also referred to a dispute between the two around one-and-a-half years earlier that had resulted in police intervention, although no formal complaint was filed at that time, according to her account.Police registered a case under Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Sections 311 and 318 and other provisions of the BNS, as well as Sections 66 and 72 of the Information Technology Act.The matter subsequently reached the Calcutta High Court, which directed the police to arrest Porel. The proceedings also included allegations of criminal intimidation and other offences alongside the rape allegation. The court had further directed authorities to seize Porel's electronic devices in connection with concerns over the possible dissemination of photographs of the complainant.Porel was produced before the Chinsurah court after his arrest and was initially denied bail before being sent to judicial custody. He has now been granted bail after spending 36 days in jail, according to the ABP Ananda report.Porel has previously denied the allegations against him.The 23-year-old wicketkeeper-batter has been part of the Delhi Capitals setup since 2023, when he made his IPL debut. He scored 108 runs in four innings for the franchise during the 2026 season. Overall, he has played 35 games, scoring 769 runs at an average of 25.63 and a strike rate of 145.37, including four fifties.Porel made his first-class debut for Bengal in the 2021-22 season and has since become an established figure in the domestic circuit. He has represented Bengal in 32 first-class matches and 23 List A games.

Why was Sydney Sweeney's ad controversial?

Sophie Cunningham isn't one to stay quiet, and this week she finally weighed in on the Sydney Sweeney gambling ad controversy that's had social media buzzing for days. The Indiana Fever guard tackled the topic on her podcast, calling out the campaign while still leaving room to defend Sweeney's right to cash in on her fame.Cunningham admitted she wasn't a fan of how the ad played out, questioning its authenticity from the jump. But she wasn't interested in piling on the actress either. Here's what she actually said, and why the ad drew so much heat in the first place.Sophie Cunningham addressed the ongoing chatter this week, tackling it head-on during an episode of her podcast, No Hesitation With Sophie Cunningham & Drew Hanlen. She said her phone had been flooded with texts and comments from people begging her to share an opinion, so she decided it was finally time.Her first question cut straight to the point: does Sweeney even gamble on sports? "Like it's just so unauthentic," she said, laying out her skepticism about the whole campaign. Cunningham wasn't shocked by how Sweeney chose to represent the brand, noting it's simply the kind of marketing the actress has built her career on."I have so many takes, but first of all, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it's just so inauthentic.Now, here's my hot take… Why are girls mad? Like, that is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? Like… of course that's going to draw attention,” the Fever guard shared.Still, she made clear she wasn't thrilled with this particular execution, admitting she wondered what exactly the ad was trying to accomplish. Again, do I agree with it? “Morally, I think it's kind of weird, but like, to each their own. Go do your thing, sis," Cunningham added.She also pushed back on the backlash itself, wondering aloud why so many women were upset over something that's essentially just Sweeney doing what she's always done. Cunningham called the outrage a little confusing, though she said she understood why some found the ad morally odd. Despite her criticism, she was quick to add that she genuinely likes Sweeney and doesn't think women should tear each other down over choices like this.Her closing message was simple: let Sweeney make her money and do her thing.The commercial in question features Sweeney posing in minimal clothing alongside sports equipment to promote a sports prediction platform, a visual pairing that got people talking almost instantly. Several athletes felt the ad leaned entirely on Sweeney's image rather than any genuine connection to sports or gambling, and that rubbed plenty of fans the wrong way.Sweeney responded to some of the criticism by sharing photos of male and female athletes who had posed n*de for ESPN The Magazine, seemingly drawing a comparison to her own shoot.

Article Title: 'We all waited for like 6 hours to get a room': D Gukesh explains why Arjun Erigaisi lost in Chess Olympiad Round 1 game
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: World champion D Gukesh has offered some context behind Arjun Erigaisi’s shock defeat in the opening round of the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, saying India’s players had endured a hectic start to the tournament and were left waiting for hours to get their rooms.Arjun, India’s second-ranked player, suffered a surprise defeat against Thailand’s 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap on Board 1. The 23-year-old, playing with the white pieces, had a winning position at different stages but eventually faltered in the endgame.Gukesh said the team’s difficult arrival and accommodation issues had affected the players.“Arjun’s first game was very unfortunate, but also worth mentioning that we had a very hectic travel and then the first day there were some organisation issues,” Gukesh said in an interview with FIDE after his Round 3 win over Italy's Sabino Brunello.“So like Arjun got a room probably a few hours before he went. I mean, we all waited for like six hours to get a room. So obviously the first round Arjun, he was just tired and he blundered in the end.”The world champion added that the situation had improved since the opening day and the players were now better rested.“The first day was a bit tricky for all of us, but after that, I think we are all rested. We are all looking forward to the games and all good,” he said.India’s chess contingent faced an unexpected accommodation crisis after arriving in Samarkand for the 46th Chess Olympiad, with several players forced to wait for hours as their hotel reservations had not been properly communicated by the local organising committee.The team was eventually accommodated at the Silk Road by Minyoun hotel after AICF president Nitin Narang intervened.Narang said the AICF took up the matter strongly with both the LOC and FIDE and made it clear that the situation was unacceptable.“In very simple terms, it was communicated that this was not acceptable and that this situation should never have happened in the first place,” Narang told TimesofIndia.com . He added, “But I am relieved that the players have now been accommodated and are finally in their rooms.”Gukesh was also asked about India’s decision to field him on Board 4, rather than the top board. He said the team’s priority was to choose the order that gave India the best chance of winning the tournament.“I think it’s pretty clear that Pragg and Arjun have been in really good shape. Also, the rating says the same,” Gukesh said. “It was my idea and also the whole team, we all thought the same that this is the order that gives us the best chance of winning the tournament.”ALSO READ: Chess Olympiad Round 3: Koneru Humpy downs 'Greek Goddess' Tsolakidou; Gukesh back above 2700 The 20-year-old said he had no issue with playing on Board 4 despite being the reigning world champion, stressing that the team’s interests came first.“If the team needs it, I would even rest all the games. So I think we are here playing for India and there’s no player bigger than the country. I’m just happy to do whatever it takes for the team to do well,” he said.India, still unbeaten in both sections, will next face Spain in the open section, while the Indian women’s team will take on Mongolia in the Round 4 on Saturday.
Article Summary: World champion D Gukesh says India's players endured a hectic start to the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Arjun Erigaisi suffered a surprise defeat against Thailand’s 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap on Board 1. India, next face Spain in the open section, while the women will take on Spain on Saturday.

Article Text:
On Friday, commuters were hit with steep increases in app-cab fares due to a city-wide halt in public transport for Vishwakarma Puja

Vishawakarama puja: 30-min wait for 20-min ride





KOLKATA: Commuters across the city faced a fare surge in app-cab services of different aggregators on Friday when a major portion of public transport, like buses, autos and metered taxis, stayed off roads because of Vishwakarma Puja. An octogenarian was charged Rs 155 for a 2.7km ride between Haltu and Gariahat, a distance of 2.7km.Booking taxis, too, took longer, and some commuters had to wait 30 minutes for an aggregator to confirm a ride that would take 20 minutes. A few spells of rain on Friday added to commuters’ woes.The app-cab aggregators attributed the soaring fares to scarcity of driver partners who mostly remained off duty due to the festival. The availability of cabs dipped further later in the day and the fare reportedly jumped after sunset.On her return home from Park Street in the afternoon, Alipore resident Aparajita Banerjee had tried booking a cab for 30 minutes, and then had to pay Rs 70 extra. “I had to go to office and am usually dependent on cabs for my commute. The fairs were higher on Friday and booking time took longer. I got a cab after waiting for 30 minutes, and then had to pay Rs 200 instead of the usual Rs 130,” she said.Around 2pm, the app cab aggregators asked for Rs 418-Rs 536 for the 15km distance from Esplanade to the airport; Rs 487- Rs 519 for the 11km from Behala Chowrasta to Esplanade; Rs 266-Rs 300 for the 6km from Janbazar to RG Kar Hospital. Around 5.30pm, the aggregators charged Rs 150-Rs 178 for 3km, between Esplanade and SSKM Hospital.Muskan Khatun, a college student who failed to get a bus to travel from Esplanade to Jadavpur 8B Bus Stand, said, “I tried booking a cab but the fare was Rs 650. It is usually within Rs 350 on other days. Finally, I took the metro and had to break the commute into shorter trips to return home.”“The fare between Baranagar and Garden Reach is usually Rs 350 but I had to pay Rs 600 on Friday,” said Baranagar resident Shreya Das.Madhyamgram resident Agnik Chatterjee said, “I had to go to Park Street from Madhyamgram, and had to pay Rs 600 — double of what I pay on other days.”Bamangachi resident Brishti Majumdar paid Rs 1,400 to travel to Park Street. “The fare is usually Rs 800, but I had to pay Rs 600 more on Friday,” she said.According to Online Cab Operators Guild, about 40% of its fleet —nearly 10,500 cabs —stayed off roads. “Usually, fewer cabs ply on Vishwakarma Puja. But on Friday, apart from the festival, the bad weather was another factor behind the fare inflation. A few private aggregators tried to capitalise on the situation, leading to over 15% hike in fares across all sectors,” said Indranil Banerjee, the general secretary of the union.The CITU-backed union conceded that not more than 50% of its workforce was on the road on Friday.(Inputs from Dwaipayan Ghosh)
Article Summary: On Friday, commuters were hit with steep increases in app-cab fares due to a city-wide halt in public transport for Vishwakarma Puja. Booking taxis, too, took longer, and some commuters had to wait 30 minutes for an aggregator to confirm a ride that would take 20 minutes. A few spells of rain on Friday added to commuters’ woes.
